key_insight: AA-ViT uses anatomy-aware attention plus structural and frequency cues to synthesize contrast-enhanced brain MRI from non-contrast inputs. This aims to make tumour-visible MRI more accessible when contrast agents cannot be used.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of generating high-quality contrast-enhanced brain MRI without administering chemical contrast agents, which may be unsafe or infeasible for some patients. It targets improved tumour localization and lesion visibility in MRI synthesis.
method: Builds a Vision Transformer architecture that is anatomically aware, so the model can better respect brain structure during synthesis.
Incorporates structural guidance to preserve anatomical consistency and reduce unrealistic generated details.
Adds frequency guidance to better capture fine image textures and contrast patterns important for lesion visibility.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work shows how domain-specific priors can be embedded into transformer-based image synthesis to improve clinical realism and usefulness. It is especially relevant for medical imaging tasks where data quality, safety, and anatomical correctness matter.

paper_title: AA-ViT: Anatomically Aware Vision Transformer with Structural and Frequency Guidance for Contrast Enhanced Brain MRI Synthesis
paper_authors: Talha Meraj, Tom Flannery, Charlie Cummins, Matt Townend, Thomas C Booth
